Anodyne

AN-uh-dyne · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Anodyne is not likely to offend or provoke strong feeling; deliberately bland.

The company's anodyne press release avoided any mention of the actual controversy.

Worked Example

Asked about the scandal, the senator gave only an anodyne comment about 'looking forward, not backward.'

The senator's comment was carefully designed to say nothing that could upset anyone, which is exactly anodyne.

How Anodyne Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

bland

bland: lacking any strong or distinctive quality

inoffensive

inoffensive: not likely to upset anyone

Antonyms

explosive

explosive: likely to trigger a strong, angry reaction

How Strong Is It? — mild → anodyne → toothless

mild vs. anodyne

mild vs. anodyne: A mild comment simply avoids taking a strong side; an anodyne one is intentionally engineered to offend no one at all.

toothless vs. anodyne

toothless vs. anodyne: An anodyne statement carefully avoids controversy; a toothless one goes further, saying almost nothing of substance at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — an-

prefix — an-: without (Greek)

root — odyne

root — odyne: pain (Greek (odyne))

Put it together

Put it together: Anodyne comes from Greek an- ('without') + odyne ('pain') -- it originally described a pain-relieving medicine, and later came to describe words or ideas designed to 'relieve' controversy by avoiding it.

Use the root in a new word: anemia

Use the root in a new word: anemia: The same privative an- prefix ('without') appears in anemia (an- + haima, 'blood' -- literally 'without blood').
